reviews.title: Culture shift needed IMMENSELY
reviews.text: Can we PLEASE normalize NOT SPOILING GAMES IN RERUNS/ENCORES??? Ffs cbj v wild is AIRING and ON THE NHL NETWORK you have the AUDACITY TO HAVE THE FINAL SCORE IN THE CORNER. STOP. LET ME ENJOY THE GAME BLIND. I am SO sick of having games spoiled for me just by virtue of being on the channel THAT IT IS AIRING ON. I follow a lot of teams, which means I don’t always get to watch games live. WHY ARE THE CASTERS TALKING ABOUT GAMES THAT JUST ENDED. WHY ARE YOU SPOILING THEM. If I wanted to know the final result, I would look it up. Stop force-feeding it to me WHILE THE GAME IS ON. I am literally having to cover the bottom of my tv right now because the final score is just sitting there with a rotating banner of who scored. The game has been ruined for me. I already know the outcome. Thank you for ruining the experience. I now know that the rest of the re-airs that I watch will also be spoiled DURING THE AIRING OF THE GAME. smh. I’ve noticed this in other sports as well and it is equally ridiculous. Just put a little “team vs team has ended. Check [sports league] for the score”! Utterly ridiculous that this is the norm. Very disappointed, especially as I have only recently gotten back into sports and have finally found one that I enjoy watching. Good to know that if I’m not paying $80 FOR ACCESS TO THE GAMES LIVE, I will be subjected to an intentionally spoiled experience.

reviews.title: Great League, Bad App
reviews.text:
Please fix the Apple TV app. There are too many basic playback bugs for an app representing a major professional sports league.

Videos often start at the end instead of the beginning. The scroll/progress bar sometimes never disappears, leaving the entire video with a dark tint over it. Those are just a couple examples, but the overall Apple TV experience is frustrating and unreliable.

I have been trying to get friends into hockey and recommended the app as a good place to start. Unfortunately, the feedback I have received, and what I have seen firsthand, is that the app is a poor experience.

If the league is serious about growing the game, the app needs to feel professional, polished, and easy to use. With the amount of sponsorship money visible across the league, there is no excuse for such a rough product. The NFL would never tolerate an app experience this bad, and the NHL should not either.
